---
title: "roomANC"
subtitle: "Whole-room active noise cancellation of tonal low-frequency HVAC noise"
---

## The problem

A rental unit suffers a constant low-frequency drone from rooftop
HVAC units and pumps. The goal of this project is to **deploy an active noise
cancellation (ANC) system — hardware and software — that cancels highly tonal
low-frequency noise** in a bedroom/living space, within the constraints of a
rental: no structural modification, nothing attached to the building fabric
beyond caulk and weatherstripping. Landlord escalation runs as a parallel track;
the measurement data this system produces supports both.

## Why this is physically feasible

Below the Schroeder frequency $f_S \approx 2000\sqrt{T_{60}/V}$ — where
$T_{60}$ is the reverberation time in seconds and $V$ the room volume in
m³ — the sound field in a room is **modal**, not diffuse. For a typical
bedroom ($V \approx 50\ \mathrm{m^3}$, $T_{60} \approx 0.4\ \mathrm{s}$),
$f_S \approx 180\ \mathrm{Hz}$. In the modal regime, a handful of room modes
carry the field, and controlling their amplitudes with a few loudspeakers
yields **global** (whole-room) cancellation — not just a small quiet zone
around a microphone. Combined with the fact that the offending noise is a few
stable tones well below $f_S$, this is exactly the regime where ANC works:
the commercial precedent is engine-order cancellation in car cabins.

Expected performance: **10–20 dB reduction at the tones** across most of the
room, with little effect on the broadband floor. Passive treatment can't
compete at these frequencies — see [Physics](physics.qmd) for why.

## Project structure

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Physics](physics.qmd) | Why the modal regime enables global ANC, why passive absorption and blocking fail below ~150 Hz, the structure-borne diagnostic, and modal geometry. |
| [Measurements](measurements.qmd) | Measured spectra and the tone census: a dominant 59.0 Hz machine tone ~56 dB above the floor, plus a 39.9 Hz source and 120 Hz mains hum. |
| [Specification](spec.qmd) | Numbered, testable system requirements; architecture; the multichannel FxLMS controller design with full equations; measurement and verification plan. |
| [Bill of Materials](bom.qmd) | Every critical component at three price points (Budget / Mid / Reference), the selected build, and supporting items. |
| [Layout](layout.qmd) | Positioning plan for the real 14′7″ × 12′ room: a 6-mic perimeter error array, 2 subwoofers expanding to 4, the room-mode coincidences, near-field exclusion, the feedback question, and mic mounting. |
| [Modes](modes.qmd) | Rectangular modal model: all 29 modes to 150 Hz vs. the measured tones, modeled pressure fields at 59.0 and 39.9 Hz with predicted nulls, and the numerical observability score of the 6-mic array. |
